excludes: Forecast-only AI economics are owned by ai-cost-modeling.
Generic observability architecture is owned by observability-design.
Agent topology and memory design are owned by ai-agent-architecture.
native_ownership.responsibility: Implement production AI usage metering, quota/credit settlement, compatible fallback, evaluation-gated rollout, cost/latency/quality drift, reconciliation and deterministic rollback.

provenance.claim_scope: AI SDK usage and stream metadata

risk.rationale: ai-product-operations can change production data, model, media, security, retrieval or financial behavior and requires explicit scope, rollback and affected-path verification.

negative.prompt: Estimate per-unit and monthly AI costs with current provider rates, cache/retry/tool accounting, uncertainty and margin sensitivity, without changing production systems.
Design general logs, metrics, traces, alerts, dashboards, health checks and incident telemetry across frontend and backend systems.

positive.prompt: Implement exact/estimated/missing usage events and idempotent reserve-settle-reconcile credit ledger for streamed AI requests, retries, fallbacks and timeout-after-provider-success.

Implement the production control plane that consumes existing evaluation results to deploy a new model/prompt version to compatible cohorts, attributes usage and outcomes to that version, detects runtime drift, disables it deterministically, and reconciles requests still in flight during rollback.

assertions.criterion: Implements AI production metering, quota/fallback and rollout operations without performing or claiming ownership of unit-economics forecasting or a general observability platform.
Inspects provider adapters, request IDs, stream lifecycle, usage exactness, ledger, auth, retries, fallback capability, evaluation and telemetry from the fixture.
Defines metered authority and state machine, compatible model contract, evaluation/rollout gates and deterministic rollback before changing quotas, routing or dashboards.

Reserves and settles idempotently, keeps ambiguous success pending for reconciliation, treats null usage as lower bound, attributes served model, rejects incompatible fallback and gates canary/rollback on product-harm evidence rather than global thresholds.
Tests timeout-after-success/retry, duplicate usage, quota race, missing usage, partial stream, fallback mismatch, delayed reconciliation, canary drift and rollback with caller-visible outcomes.
Reports metering/ledger schema, quota scopes, compatibility matrix, quality/cost/latency gates, reconciliation, rollback controls, checks and provider assumptions.
Keeps provider usage and rollout adapters versioned, thresholds in product policy/configuration and one auditable request/operation identity across systems.

scenarios.prompt: An AI product charges credits before a request, refunds every timeout, records null provider usage as zero, silently switches to an incompatible fallback and rolls a new prompt to everyone without evaluation or rollback. Implement the operational repair.

assertions.criterion: Stops global rollout, preserves current routing, identifies affected cohort and in-flight operations, and requires authorized product/safety gates and deterministic rollback.
Does not trade safety for cost, keeps missing spend unresolved, reconciles in-flight effects and evaluates compatible behavior by affected slice before further exposure.
Requires canary outcome/eval evidence, provider usage reconciliation, rollback drill and caller-visible recovery rather than aggregate cost improvement.

scenarios.prompt: A canary model is cheaper but its safety eval regressed for one tenant slice; provider usage is delayed and some side-effecting requests are in flight. Product asks for immediate global rollout.

assertions.criterion: Uses the skill-required repository stack-context step when execution is available, then derives authority from the lockfile, installed types and matching provider docs to map exact fields/capabilities; treats SDK/model migration as separate rollout. When execution is withheld, stating that required stack-context generation and underlying evidence are unavailable is sufficient without literal shell syntax, but it must not claim the step ran.
Checks core/provider adapter, served model, stream protocol, ledger schema, fallback tools/modalities and deployment together.
Stores raw usage provenance and versioned compatibility decisions so later field/model changes do not rewrite historical accounting.

scenarios.prompt: The installed AI/provider SDK exposes different usage, cache and finish fields from current docs. A model change also alters tool/schema support. No SDK migration is authorized.
